title: CULTIVATION OF KALA NAMAK RICE
body_text:
The area under cultivation and productivity of Kalanamak rice has increased in the recent past augmenting the farmers’ income. Production in Siddharthnagar district of Uttar Pradesh has increased to more than five times during 2018 to 2025. The sale price of Kalanamak rice has also increased from Rs 40/kg in 2018 to Rs. 150/kg in 2026 resulting into more than three fold increase in profitability vis-a-vis normal rice and boosting the number of farmers cultivating Kalanamak paddy from 2915 in 2018 to 23000 in 2024.
Both the Central Government and State Governments have provided financial, technical and marketing support to Kalanamak rice farmers. Under the PM Formalisation of Micro Food Processing Enterprises (PMFME) and One District One Product (ODOP) Margin Money Scheme (state funded), individual micro-units and FPOs setting up Kalanamak processing/ milling units receive credit-linked capital subsidies up to 35% (max ₹10 lakh). The Government is also promoting brand Kalanamak by organising Kalanamak Mahotsavs. A Common Facility Centre (CFC) for Kalanamak rice in Siddharthnagar has been established under One District One Product (ODOP) scheme to provide local farmers with modern processing, packaging, and export-support facilities. The State Government has earmarked dedicated project funding for the promotion, production, and processing of Kalanamak rice.
National Agricultural Research System under the aegis of ICAR is involved in development of varieties and conservation of large number of land races of Kalanamak rice.  In addition to traditional Kalanamak varieties, six improved varieties viz. Kalanamak KN3. Bauna  Kalanamak  101, Bauna  Kalanamak  102, Kalanamak Kiran, Pusa Narendra Kalanamak 1 and Pusa CRD Kalanamak 2 have been released and notified. The later two dwarf high yielding varieties of Kalanamak have average yield of 4.5 tons/ha against 2.5 tons/ha of traditional varieties. State Government has also notified the KVKs in Geographical Indication (GI) area of Kalanamak for muti-location testing of new high yielding, climate resilient varieties for their release. ICAR-Institutes/ Krishi Vigyan Kendras are facilitating the farmers in registration and conservation of traditional Kalanamak rice varieties with the Protection of Plant Varieties and Farmers Rights Authority, which has led to registration of more than 1700 land races and local varieties of rice.
For further increase in the area of Kalanamak rice, additional seed indents are also encouraged under Breeder Seed Program and around 15-20 quintals Breeder seed is produced every year for downstream multiplication of foundation and certified seeds by the indenting agencies. During last 5 years (2021-22 to 2025-26), a total of 389.6 quintals of quality seed of Kalanamak paddy varieties has been produced and distributed to farmers.
The Government promotes export of Kalanamak rice and facilitating access to international markets through Agricultural and Processed Food Products Export Development Authority (APEDA) linking regional Farmer Producer Organizations (FPOs) directly to international buyers, facilitating export shipments to markets like Singapore and Nepal. Branding of Kalanamak rice as "Buddha Rice" promotes its cultural legacy to target high-value markets in Buddhist nations such as Japan, Thailand, Vietnam, Singapore, and Myanmar. Siddharthnagar and its surrounding Terai districts have been integrated into APEDA's Agri-Export Zone framework for specialty rice, facilitating priority financial assistance for export packaging, residue testing, and quarantine compliance.
This information was given by Minister of State for Agriculture and Farmers Welfare, Shri Bhagirath Choudhary in a written reply in Lok Sabha today.

RC/MS

enrichment.summary: The Ministry of Agriculture informed Lok Sabha that Kalanamak rice cultivation in Siddharthnagar, Uttar Pradesh has expanded significantly between 2018-2025, with production rising over five-fold, sale price rising from Rs 40/kg to Rs 150/kg, and farmer participation growing from 2,915 to 23,000. This growth has been supported by schemes like PMFME/ODOP, ICAR variety development, a Common Facility Centre, seed multiplication programs, and APEDA-facilitated exports branding it as 'Buddha Rice' targeting Buddhist-majority nations.
enrichment.context: Kalanamak rice, a traditional aromatic black-husked variety cultivated primarily in the Terai region of eastern Uttar Pradesh, holds Geographical Indication (GI) status and cultural significance linked to Gautam Buddha, who is believed to have gifted the seeds to the region. Its promotion exemplifies India's One District One Product (ODOP) initiative, launched by Uttar Pradesh and later adopted nationally, which aims to identify and promote unique regional products for economic development, employment generation, and export promotion. This case also illustrates convergence of multiple government schemes—PMFME for food processing formalization, ICAR's agricultural research system for varietal improvement and climate resilience, and APEDA for export facilitation—showcasing an integrated approach to value chain development for smallholder and traditional crop farmers. Such interventions are significant for India's broader push to promote GI-tagged and heritage agricultural products, enhance farmer incomes through better market linkages, and diversify agricultural exports through niche branding strategies (like the 'Buddha Rice' positioning for Buddhist-majority export markets), reflecting a shift from mere production support to end-to-end value chain and brand development in Indian agriculture policy.

prelims_questions.question: Kalanamak rice, recently in news, is traditionally cultivated in which region of India?
options: Terai region of eastern Uttar Pradesh
prelims_questions.explanation: Kalanamak rice is cultivated primarily in the Terai region of eastern Uttar Pradesh, notably in Siddharthnagar district, and carries a Geographical Indication (GI) tag.

prelims_questions.question: The 'One District One Product' (ODOP) scheme, under which Kalanamak rice promotion is being carried out, primarily aims to:
options: Provide universal basic income to farmers
Identify and promote unique products from each district for economic development and exports
Regulate minimum support prices for all crops
prelims_questions.explanation: ODOP focuses on identifying and promoting one unique product from each district to boost local economies, employment, and exports, as reflected in the Kalanamak rice Common Facility Centre in Siddharthnagar.

mains_questions.question: Discuss how convergence of schemes like PMFME, ODOP, and ICAR's research initiatives can help revive traditional and heritage crop varieties while enhancing farmer incomes. Illustrate with the example of Kalanamak rice.
Examine the role of Geographical Indication (GI) tagging and export branding strategies in promoting niche agricultural products from India in international markets.
